profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC13 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC13 is a 75,003 square foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of the operator's 15-facility Washington DC metro region. No power capacity is published for this building on its specification page. The site maintains N+20% cooling redundancy, a configuration typical of colocation infrastructure built for high availability rather than dense AI training loads.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1,375 MW. This facility does not contribute to the published count because Equinix has not disclosed DC13's megawatt rating. The Ashburn cluster is positioned as the largest peering point in North America and a gateway to Europe, a role centered on network traffic and enterprise colocation rather than on the contiguous power blocks required for GPU scaling.

Without published power figures for individual Ashburn facilities, the contribution of DC13 to AI infrastructure capacity cannot be assessed from operator disclosures. The lack of megawatt transparency across Equinix's Washington DC campus—despite the region's strategic importance—means this site's actual binding constraint for GPU deployments remains unknown from public sources.
